review.note: Extracted as text from the old lesson, then reviewed against the verified dataset. A line with "review" set is held (not shown) until a teacher resolves it. Dropped: the five Tajweed rules, the two Tajweed games and the Tajweed quiz question (Tajweed comes only from the reviewed dataset), the audio URLs and the reciter line, and every hand-typed Quran string (replaced by positions). The complete-the-ayah words are the answers of the old "complete the ayah" and "missing word" games; the two-word answers (humazatin lumazah, malan wa-'addadah) became their last word, and the games' hand-typed distractors (none of them words of this surah) are gone: the game draws its options from these words. Two old spellings needed a matching-only aid, never stored: adraka (5:2, Uthmani adraka with alif maqsura and dagger alif) and al-af'idah (7:4, Uthmani writes its hamza without the ya seat). One word meaning ('addadahu) was typed without the "wa-" the verse word carries; it points at the whole verse word (2:4). The old quiz had difficulty levels (easy, medium, hard), not categories; the categories were assigned by question type. Each lesson learned is its old title and description joined with ": ". The reflection is the old prompt's question, with the "how we apply these lessons" tips as its ideas. Not carried (no field or no such game in the engine): the "Makki" type, the "why it was revealed" line, the ayah-ordering, start-end memory and choose-the-ayah games, the three word-meaning games (same words and meanings as the list), the intro quiz (surah name, ayah count), the reflection's lead-in line, its three "will you ..." prompts and its closing du'a.

intro.text: سورة الهُمَزَة سورة مكية نزلت في مكة المكرمة، عدد آياتها 9 آيات. تتحدث عن الذي يعيب الناس ويغتابهم ويظن أن ماله سيبقيه للأبد.

tafsir.text: عذاب شديد لكل من يعيب الناس بالكلام أو بالإشارة. يعني لا نتكلم عن الناس بكلام سيء!
هذا الشخص يجمع المال ويعدّه كثيرًا ويفرح به. لكن المال وحده لا يكفي!
يظن أن ماله الكثير سيجعله يعيش للأبد! لكن هذا غير صحيح، الله وحده هو الباقي.
لا! سيُلقى في نار شديدة تسمى الحُطَمة. هذا عقاب من لا يطيع الله.
tafsir.review: Ends "this is the punishment of whoever does not obey Allah". The ayah threatens the man of ayat 1-3 (the slanderer who hoards wealth and thinks it makes him immortal); as written a child may take it that every disobedience leads to al-Hutamah. Teacher to reword.

tafsir.text: هل تعرف ما هي الحُطَمة؟ إنها نار عظيمة جدًا! الله يخبرنا عنها لنحذر.
هي نار الله المشتعلة التي لا تنطفئ أبدًا.
هذه النار تصل إلى القلوب. نسأل الله أن يحمينا منها.
هذه النار مغلقة عليهم ولا يستطيعون الخروج منها.
في أعمدة طويلة ممتدة. نسأل الله السلامة.

words.review: One view (Mujahid, Ibn Zayd): humazah faults people by gesture (hand, eye), lumazah by the tongue. Others reverse it, or say both are the backbiter and slanderer (Ibn Abbas: humazah lumazah, the one who goes about backbiting and defaming). Teacher to choose the wording.

quiz.question: ما أول كلمة في سورة الهمزة؟
quiz.review: CHANGED: the old distractors "qul" and "bismi" were hand-typed Quran not of this surah; they are now the first words of ayat 3 and 4 (yahsabu, kalla). The answer (waylun, 1:1) and the fourth option (alladhi, 2:1) are unchanged.

quiz.question: ماذا يظن الشخص الذي يجمع المال؟
ما الدرس المستفاد من سورة الهمزة؟

options.text: لا نغتاب الناس ولا نسخر منهم

quiz.question: أكمل الآية
quiz.review: CHANGED: the old distractors were invented words (umazah, humazah with ha, rumazah), not Quran; they are now mumaddadah (9:3), al-hutamah (4:4) and mu'sadah (8:3), words of this surah. The answer (lumazah, 1:4) is unchanged.

quiz.question: أكمل
quiz.review: CHANGED: the old distractors (a'tahu, afrahahu, akramahu) were hand-typed, not of this surah; they are now 'addadahu (2:4), adraka (5:2) and jama'a (2:2), words of this surah. The answer (akhladahu, 3:4) is unchanged.

lessons.text: لا نغتاب الناس: لا نتكلم عن الناس بكلام سيء من ورائهم
لا نسخر من أحد: لا نضحك على الناس أو نعيبهم
المال ليس كل شيء: الأخلاق الطيبة أهم من المال الكثير
نكون طيبين: نتكلم بكلام جميل ونعامل الناس بلطف
نشكر الله: نشكر الله على كل النعم ولا نتكبر
lessons.review: Gratitude is not a theme of this surah; the "do not be arrogant" half fits (the man who trusts his wealth). Teacher to keep, reword or drop.

lessons.text: نطيع الله: نسمع كلام الله ورسوله ونبتعد عما نهانا عنه
lessons.review: A good lesson (obey Allah and His Messenger), but not one this surah teaches. Teacher to keep or drop.

reflection.question: ما أجمل شيء تعلمته من سورة الهمزة؟
ideas: نتكلم بكلام جميل عن الناس ولا نغتابهم
نشكر الله على نعمه ولا نتكبر بما عندنا
نكون لطيفين مع أصدقائنا ولا نسخر من أحد

didYouKnow.text: سورة الهمزة هي السورة رقم 104 في القرآن الكريم
كلمة 'الحُطَمة' هي اسم من أسماء النار
قراءة القرآن كل يوم تجعلك قريبًا من الله
كل حرف تقرأه من القرآن لك به حسنة والحسنة بعشر أمثالها
الهُمَزة هو الذي يعيب الناس بالإشارة واللُّمَزة بالكلام
didYouKnow.review: One view (Mujahid, Ibn Zayd): humazah faults people by gesture (hand, eye), lumazah by the tongue. Others reverse it, or say both are the backbiter and slanderer (Ibn Abbas: humazah lumazah, the one who goes about backbiting and defaming). Teacher to choose the wording.

didYouKnow.text: سورة الهمزة نزلت في مكة المكرمة
من يحفظ القرآن يكون من أهل الله وخاصته
didYouKnow.review: The hadith (Ahmad, Ibn Majah, from Anas) says "ahl al-Quran are the people of Allah and His elect"; the scholars explain ahl al-Quran as those who memorise it AND act by it, not memorising alone. Teacher to confirm the wording.

didYouKnow.text: النبي ﷺ قال: خيركم من تعلم القرآن وعلمه
